function: above_phy, p. 7: model-free RL decides whether an access satellite serves each user (user access action), feeding a matching game that associates users, LEO access satellites, and backhaul destination nodes.
notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3368327 are on p. 1, so the PDF matches. Learning is part of the method, not only motivation or baseline (RL 'training' results, Fig. 3, p. 10), so no_learning does not apply. The RL acts above the PHY: its action is the access satellite's decision 'whether to provide data collection services to the user, i.e., whether to establish a preference relationship' (p. 7), its reward is 'the degree of completeness of the preference list' (p. 7), and 'the action is transmitted to the matching game algorithm for outputting the resource allocation results' (p. 8). The 'resource allocation' of problem P0 has only binary link variables, user to access satellite and access satellite to destination node, a GEO relay or a ground station (p. 5, p. 3): user association, access control, and backhaul routing. Transmit power and bandwidth are given parameters (p. 3) and no beam is designed, so the satellite exception for learned power, resource allocation, or beam control was considered and not applied. Metrics are matched users, AS revenue, user satisfaction, iterations, and time (p. 10). The paper says RL is applied 'to predict and approach the complete network channel state information' (p. 5), but the MDP on p. 7 estimates or predicts no channel quantity. Reviewer to confirm above_phy against an area 6 reading.
